key_idea: The cost of using store v is d(1,v)+d(v,n); she uses the cheapest stocked store, so sort stores by that cost and sum cost * p * product of (1-p) of all cheaper stores.
sketch: Run Dijkstra from 1 and from n, giving each store a detour cost c_v. Sort stores by c_v; the probability that store i is the one used is p_i times the product of (1 - p_j) over cheaper stores, so the expectation is one linear pass. It is impossible exactly when no store has p = 1 (otherwise all stores can be empty with positive probability); once a store with p = 1 is reached the remaining probability is zero. O((n + m) log n + k log k). Pitfalls: detect p = 1 exactly by parsing to an integer number of 1e-4 units, use long double for the product, and distances up to 2e11 need 64-bit.
